LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen hard and is sitting near its lowest point of the past year — the real issue is that its profit margins have slipped well below where they used to be, though defense spending itself remains a steady tailwind.

ASML.sentence: ASML is quiet this week, and while its price looks expensive against last year's earnings, that's expected to normalize as a wave of AI-driven chipmaking demand lifts profits into 2026.

LIN.sentence: Linde is ticking up gently — industrial gas demand is steady and the business is doing fine, it's just priced in line with its peers right now rather than at the usual premium.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm, with the AI cloud story grinding along steadily — the big test comes with their late-October earnings, when everyone will be watching whether Azure keeps growing fast enough.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher dipped a little, but biotech funding is thawing and that money tends to turn into lab-equipment orders a few quarters down the road, which is good for them.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is steady — its pipelines work like toll roads and pay a generous dividend, though the stock looks fairly priced rather than a bargain right now.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow is down from its highs but recovering faster than its software rivals, as big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow-automation and AI tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore is up slightly and paying a generous dividend, with its commodity-trading arm providing a reliable cushion even when mining prices swing around.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta edged up, and the key number — the price it gets per ton of rock — is still climbing nicely, confirming that each quarry's local grip on its market is fully intact.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is quiet, with a stable Mexican peso and nothing much moving the bottling business this week.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras slipped a touch, but with oil prices far above what it costs them to pump, their big dividend is comfortably covered.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, is trading for less than it would cost to replace its own fleet of ships — a classic sign of a cyclical business being priced cheaply at a low point.

MA.sentence: Mastercard barely moved and now trades at the same price level as Visa, even though it's the faster-growing of the two — people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot maker dipped slightly but is cheaper relative to its own history than it's been in years, while hospitals keep steadily increasing the number of robot-assisted operations they perform.
